learner_operation: Read both signed summands, identify their exponents, increase each exponent by one and divide by the new exponent, then combine both antiderivatives and one arbitrary constant. For radio, distinguish this result from errors in signs, powers, factors or constants.

fixed_features.feature: Two summands and elementary power-rule antiderivatives, with p != -1
fixed_features.justification: e-371 and tutorial 701 establish sum splitting; prerequisites supply monomial, radical and reciprocal power rules. Excluding logarithms preserves scope.
Target KP examples use this structure; tutorial 703 and the next KP introduce nontrivial constant-factor workload.

fixed_features.feature: Five-choice radio or the derivative blank with external +C
fixed_features.justification: Captured q-71167/q-71169 and q-133291 response contracts.

counterfactuals.change: Change polynomial/blank or reciprocal exponent, sign or constant, holding other eligible data fixed. Reciprocal exponent 3 -> 7 changes the answer from -2/sqrt(x)+4x+C to -2/(5sqrt(x^5))+4x+C.
counterfactuals.expected: Both transformed answer and power-rule solution must follow the changed integrand; exactly the newly correct choice/blank must grade accepted.
counterfactuals.observed: All 7 original and 6 additional pairs have expected semantic equality/change relationships. Exact text-derived differentiation, 733 native checks and rendered before/after pairs agree.
counterfactuals.justification: Tutorial 701 and e-371 require independent integration of both signed summands.

counterfactuals.change: Reorder summands, consistently rename variable, or change only the competing divisor in the answer bank.
counterfactuals.expected: Preserve the mathematical response under reordering/renaming; preserve the same antiderivative when distractors change.
counterfactuals.observed: Passed all applicable semantic comparisons, native accepted/rejected checks and visual pairs, including P_competitor_side.
counterfactuals.justification: Sum rule and commutativity do not depend on printed summand order or notation; distractors do not alter the integrand.

counterfactuals.change: Keep integral 5-x^3, correct answer 5x-x^4/4+C and solution fixed; omit the wrong-power choice from the true constant row instead of from a wrong constant row.
counterfactuals.expected: Five distinct choices and the same unique antiderivative; singleton status may belong to the correct constant because it has no integration meaning.
counterfactuals.observed: Independent control has five distinct choices, one correct derivative, same prompt/solution, passes shared delivery and native grader, and renders correctly. Current generator rejects omitted_row=0, omitted_col=1, unnecessarily fixing the singleton row as wrong.
counterfactuals.justification: Neither tutorial 701 nor q-71167/q-71169 imposes a frequency role on a correct constant coefficient. Excluding this assignment creates the demonstrated cue.

shortcut_probes.cue: Frequency of the displayed linear coefficient across choices
shortcut_probes.strategy: Eliminate the choice whose linear coefficient occurs only once; choose uniformly from the remaining four. No prompt inspection or integration.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Uniform choice among five has baseline 0.20. The cue always eliminates one wrong option, giving exact 0.25 expected success (25% relative advantage), independently of numerical parameters or option order. Seeded empirical success is 60/226; this is a partial shortcut, not a claim of perfect answer prediction. Four exhaustive omitted-cell graphs prove the advantage.

stages_examined: generator prechoice constraints and absence of rejection/resampling
publisher validation and stable identity normalization
difficulty weights and SHA256 selection with explicit synthetic policies/history
delivery.result: 360 ->329 fresh accepted records (31 duplicates), runner5 ->5; singleton cue survives every delivered radio and selected generated radio. No publication preparation existed; actual shared read-only filtering used captured basis 5277. No database writes.

limitations: No finite audit proves absence of all shortcuts.
Selection uses captured usable bank, synthetic new entity IDs and explicit policy/history scenarios; live policy, IDs, history and future inventory changes are not captured.
Unconfigured policy selects smallest usable ID and may deliver only existing source items; zero moderate weight excludes this generator by design.

The R3 even-numerator exploratory probe has an observed advantage, but no separate defect is asserted from numerical recognition of its mathematically forced coefficient 2; the reported failure uses only answer-bank multiplicity and does not require fixed-exponent recall.
Missing source keys/solutions and fields are documented in source-analysis.json; no response fields are invented for math-only replay families.
